summary_en: This Phase 2 study compares standard androgen receptor blockade (apalutamide or enzalutamide) with and without carotuximab in patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer that has progressed on an androgen receptor signaling inhibitor. Apalutamide or enzalutamide is taken by mouth once daily on days 1 to 28 of each 28-day cycle, and carotuximab is given intravenously, with escalating doses in cycle 1 and 15 mg/kg every 4 weeks after cycle 2. The main outcome measured is progression-free survival, compared between the two groups using RECIST 1.1 and Prostate Cancer Working Group 3 criteria.
summary_es: Este estudio de fase 2 compara el bloqueo estándar del receptor de andrógenos (apalutamida o enzalutamida) con y sin carotuximab en pacientes con cáncer de próstata metastásico resistente a la castración que progresó con un inhibidor de la vía del receptor de andrógenos. La apalutamida o la enzalutamida se toman por vía oral una vez al día durante los días 1 a 28 de cada ciclo de 28 días, y el carotuximab se administra por vía intravenosa, con dosis que aumentan en el ciclo 1 y de 15 mg/kg cada 4 semanas después del ciclo 2. El resultado principal que se mide es la supervivencia libre de progresión, comparada entre los dos grupos según los criterios RECIST 1.1 y del Grupo de Trabajo de Cáncer de Próstata 3.
who_for: Castration-resistant prostate cancer with rising PSA while on a contemporary androgen receptor signaling inhibitor.
PSA rise of 0.2 ng/mL or higher on at least 2 occasions more than 1 week apart.
Surgically castrated, or testosterone under 50 ng/dL while on LHRH analog therapy.
Declined or ineligible for taxane therapy, in the treating physician's opinion.
not_for: Non-PSA-producing prostate cancers, such as small cell, or radiographic progression without PSA rise.
Other prior malignancy that needs active anticancer therapy.
Prior exposure to carotuximab or any CD105-targeted antibody.
Uncontrolled high blood pressure, high bleeding risk, or acute cardiovascular event within 6 months.
Untreated brain or spinal cord involvement with cancer, or carcinomatous meningitis.
